sentences.english_text: Of course, the audience was not applauding Drippy.
To tell you the truth, they did not even know he was there.
The stage was very large, and Drippy was so small that they could not see him.
The audience was applauding the performers in the show, and what a show it was.
There were jugglers, and tightrope walkers, and acrobats, and dancing girls, and Mr. Harris, the world's greatest magician.
Drippy had never been on a stage before, and he watched in wonder as the performers came out and began to do their acts.
The tightrope walker was the first.
Drippy watched in amazement as the man climbed to the top of a rope that was stretched between two poles.
The man began to walk the rope, carefully keeping his balance.
When he reached the other end of the rope, the audience applauded.
What he's doing is nothing.
I went higher than that.
I flew through the sky with the wind.
But Drippy wished that the audience would applaud him.
When the man on the tightrope was finished and left the stage, a juggler came onto the stage.
He started throwing Indian clubs into the air, spinning them up and catching them, and spinning them up again, three at a time.
That's nothing.
I climbed up a whole statue.
Drippy was standing next to some Indian clubs that the juggler had put on the stage floor.
He decided to climb up on one of the clubs to get a better view of the audience.
Suddenly the juggler reached down and picked up the club that Drippy was on.
And Drippy found himself spinning up into the air.
He hung on to the club, not daring to let go.
I'm part of the juggler's act, Drippy thought.
He did not know whether to be sorry or glad.
Every time he was thrown into the air, Drippy wished he were back on the ground.
But each time the juggler caught the Indian club and the audience applauded, Drippy was glad he was in show business.
I'm a star.
He liked the idea.
In fact, he liked it very much.
When the juggler finished his act and took a bow, Drippy took a bow too.
He had no idea that he was so small.
That the audience could not possibly see him.
